caption:
Wide-area change detection finds what moved. It does not tell you why.

Across an area of interest, we run successive optical and radar passes against a baseline and flag deltas — new clearing, disturbed ground, structure changes, vessel presence. That cueing narrows a search area from hundreds of square kilometers to a handful of points worth a closer look.

The honest limit: a flagged change is a signature, not a verdict. It does not say who did it, whether it is licit, or what happens next. That call still needs ground truth — a patrol, a source, a follow-up collect. Treat the output as a tasking list, not a finding.
